mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.2 percentage points from the previous month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a short-term sell-off in equities as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a supply-side shock where manufacturing output is falling but housing activity is increasing, leading to temporary inflationary pressure and a 60-day decline in equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO declines and HOUST rises, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high consumer credit growth (RSAFS), the S&P 500 tends to experience positive 20-day returns as rising household spending supports corporate revenue growth, but this effect is only active in the early stages of an economic expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances during early-cycle expansion when RSAFS is rising, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 6 months indicates a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS has increased for 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3 percentage points from the previous month signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and causes a short-term decline in equity prices over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3pp, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) indicates a shift in consumer spending patterns where housing demand is falling but overall consumption is rising, leading to a 20-day positive return as the market discounts consumer sector resilience.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST declines and GDPC1 rises, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%), the S&P 500 tends to experience negative 60-day returns as the cost of capital rises and economic growth slows, but this effect is only pronounced in the late stages of an economic cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% during late-cycle, or the Rank IC is negative over a 3-year rolling window.
